_meta.indication: HYMPAVZI is a TFPI antagonist indicated for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce the frequency of bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with hemophilia A (congenital factor VIII deficiency) without factor VIII inhibitors, or hemophilia B (congenital factor IX deficiency) without factor IX inhibitors.

pivotal_trials.design: One-way, open-label, multicenter, two-phase study with a 6-month observational phase (OP) followed by a single-arm 12-month active treatment phase (ATP); no randomization, no blinding.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older (≥35 kg) with severe hemophilia A without FVIII inhibitors or severe hemophilia B without FIX inhibitors.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was the annualized bleeding rate (ABR) of treated bleeding events during HYMPAVZI treatment compared with the observational phase.
pivotal_trials.n: 116 patients received HYMPAVZI (33 in the on-demand cohort, 83 in the routine prophylaxis cohort).
pivotal_trials.result: Versus on-demand: treated-bleed ABR 3.18 (95% CI 2.09, 4.85) on HYMPAVZI vs 38.00 (31.03, 46.54); ratio 0.084 (0.059, 0.119), p<0.0001. Versus prior routine prophylaxis: treated-bleed ABR 5.08 (3.40, 6.77) vs 7.85 (5.09, 10.61); difference -2.77 (-5.37, -0.16), meeting non-inferiority.

key_safety: Adverse reactions reported in ≥3% of HYMPAVZI-treated patients (N=116) were injection site reaction 11 (9%), headache 8 (7%), and pruritus 4 (3%). Key warnings/precautions are thromboembolic events, hypersensitivity, and embryofetal toxicity.
target_moa: Marstacimab is a human IgG1 monoclonal antibody antagonist of tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI). It binds the Kunitz 2 (K2) domain of TFPI, neutralizing TFPI activity to enhance the extrinsic coagulation pathway and thrombin generation in patients with hemophilia.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee was convened; the application did not raise efficacy or safety issues requiring external expert advice.

summary.text: BLA 761369 was a standard review (priority review requested but standard timeline applied). Marstacimab held orphan drug designation (May 18, 2016) and Fast Track Designation (September 17, 2019); a Breakthrough Therapy request was denied. Approval was based on the single pivotal BASIS study (B7841005) providing substantial evidence of effectiveness.

On May 18, 2016, marstacimab received orphan drug designation for treatment of Hemophilia A and Hemophilia B patients with or without inhibitors. Fast Track Designation was granted on September 17, 2019.

The Applicant submitted results from one adequate and well-controlled clinical study (Study B7841005) that served as the equivalent of two studies, which provides substantial evidence of effectiveness (SEE) of marstacimab for the indication.
